title: Flit Physics?
author: Pure-Masterpiece-857
selftext:
Hey,

I posted about it before but my post got filtered. I ran into a lib with an mcp called Flit Physics and I don't really understand how it works. It seems fast but it's using something called morton codes? Anyway, I'm new to all this, I'm sorry.

comments.author: alcanthro
comments.body:
Morton codes are a way to put spatial information into a one dimensional indexed list for fast queries and is useful for collision detection. [https://dmytry.com/texts/collision\_detection\_using\_z\_order\_curve\_aka\_Morton\_order.html](https://dmytry.com/texts/collision_detection_using_z_order_curve_aka_Morton_order.html)

Flit seems to be using a number of different techniques, including smart simplifications, for spatial analysis and manipulation.

replies.author: Pure-Masterpiece-857
replies.body: Okay. I feel. REAL stupid. How the heck does that... Okay, I've read it, and I've had AI summarize it... What... what like, prevents it from being wrong when things are across those weird "boundaries?"

replies.author: alcanthro
replies.body: Morton order is just an easy way to search. The rest simplifies calculations to make it fast and effective on typical hardware. It's not meant to be perfect.
